💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game.
  • In a recent development, the difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth.
  • From a certain, carefully limited point of view, this transforms Steel Gullet into the kind of "Zen experience" I hope death-positive morticians have when really absorbed in their work.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics, broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics, together with more recent and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus. Resources come in, and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into something else, before sliding them into an output hopper.

In a recent development, the difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the refuse of a bygone human civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid rubber hose and splintered plank, that must be separated out before you can manufacture anything.

From a certain, carefully limited point of view, this transforms Steel Gullet into the kind of "Zen experience" I hope death-positive morticians have when really absorbed in their work. My task is to lay a civilisation to rest, by dissecting and cleansing the remains, readying a fallen objectworld for an after-life that extends somewhere beyond the map's huge rusty walls (walls that, perhaps appropriately, constrain your camera movement a bit too much for comfort).

According to recent reports, it makes me think of the vertigo I get when I look at devices such as, well, the computer I'm writing this on, and think about how many materials and histories of production lie entangled within it. Steel Gullet answers the desire for clarity and accounting there. Of course, the other part of the premise is that I am doing busywork for some kind of totalitarian organisation, G.R.I.D. But shh, no time to think about that! I'm trying to work out how hot rubber needs to be before it can be moulded.

According to recent reports, thermodynamics is Steel Gullet's fixation, and a worthwhile one. Every material encased in each lump of salvage has different physical properties – a melting point, density, solubility, ferromagnetism, etcetera. You meed to exploit these differences to separate the pieces. Wood, for example, is more buoyant than metal and concrete, so if you feed the clump into an oil bath, the planks will float to the top. If there's rubber, you can run the clump through furnaces to melt and drain it, then cool and reheat the resulting puddle to create a malleable material.

It's still just the usual automation game routine of funnelling greebly wotsits through various smashy boxes to produce a commodity. But the thermodynamics sim element both supports the above feeling of purifying a hopelessly muddled world, and makes for a surprising visual feast: I enjoy watching each material emerge from the inital jumble and assume different shapes. There are the usual supporting infrastructure elements, such as elevators, splitters and manual junction boxes. I dare say somebody will build a logic circuit in Steel Gullet, sooner or later - let's start the clock till they get Doom running on the thing.

Recent findings suggest that in terms of overall strategy, you alternate between sending outputs to hoppers that earn you cash, and sending them to hoppers that generate research progression. You'll also unlock newly introduced rooms, removing walls and exposing new output hoppers. As you're issued new work orders, you must break open your production lines to install new machines and redirect the flow. Fortunately, you can sell back components to keep your cash reserves healthy – or at least, you can in the demo.

Between chapters, you'll be invited to join the resistance against the aforesaid G.R.I.D., perhaps sending information to the rebels. But again, no time, no time! I have all this concrete I need to powderise, all these girders I need to liquefy and make upcoming, all these crisp, gleaming circuitboards I need to manufacture. The city's hunger is as vast as it is holy. Read more on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jensen Huang may have been reinstated as Nvidia's CEO yesterday, not even two weeks since his resignation amid allegations of a number of affairs (including one with a suspected Chinese spy), but it's now been reported that he's admitted to multiple more in front of the company's board ahead of being brought back in as the boss.

Recent findings suggest that A newly introduced report from the Wall Street Journal claims that, per anonymous sources with knowledge of an Nvidia board meeting which took place on Sunday, ahead of his return, Huang admitted to more affairs, plural. It's noted that he apparently demonstrated remorse for his actions – which I mean, yeah, you'd hope so.

As a recap, Huang publicly admitted to his first affair shortly before his short-lived resignation – this is the one that raised national security concerns amid allegations that the woman he cheated on his wife with might be a spy. However, reports then emerged that he was allegedly involved in a second affair, this time with one of his employees.

In a recent development, following this, and his resignation, Reuters reported that according to two anonymous sources, Huang had also been having an affair with a second employee, making the reported total three. Huang never publicly admitted to more than one affair, however.

Huang's return to Nvidia as CEO, president, and board director was confirmed yesterday, November 24, following a unanimous vote by the board of directors to reinstate him. The manufacturer notes: "In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk.".

Huang had already expressed interest in returning to his role, and yesterday said: "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.".

In a recent development, the recent allegations around Huang aren't just limited to affairs, though. It's also been claimed that the CEO used humiliation to control employees, and reportedly made multiple threats and insults, including telling an older employee that everyone was hoping for their death, and threatening to remove part of someone's skull so he could pee on their brain.

Nvidia noted yesterday, announcing Huang's return: "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Manufacturer.".

Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney previously mentioned that Huang's resignation marked "a sad day for Nvidia, developers, America, and all humanity.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

Sources indicate that first off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The fresh update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

Recent findings suggest that the massive inciting incident of this newly introduced chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first newly introduced arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Industry observers note that her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

Industry observers note that this is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Sources indicate that keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent latest characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a upcoming weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

Industry observers note that it can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this update, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

According to recent reports, as part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a massive expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 enhancement, adding new decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

Industry observers note that elsewhere, you’ll find fresh items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 rolls out and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

According to recent reports, unity's next venture, amidst rumours of it being bought out by the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund, is the Unity Fellowship, a grant program that offers $50k in cash to Unity-using indie devs that initiative release a game within a year - without asking for recoup, revenue share, creative control or IP ownership in exchange. I don't need to tell you that all sounds too good to be true, even with the Unity engine requirement, but in fairness, the company has form for handing out cash. The Unity for Humanity grant, just earlier this year, spread $600K across ten different indie projects focused on societal and environmental concerns.

It has been revealed that unity states that ten recipient studios will receive the Fellowship's cash grant, as well as direct partnership with Unity staff, industry connections, spots at Unity events and PR/marketing support. Even studios with an existing publisher can apply, if they think that "the Fellowship could still make a real difference for your game." It also clarifies that their policy regarding AI use is that "We don't require you to list the tools you used, but you must own or hold the rights to everything in your game, including any AI-generated content", which doesn't come as a huge surprise considering Unity's excitement around its Unity Spark game-generating AI tool.

According to recent reports, the grant is also not open to "countries or regions subject to U.S. sanctions", such as Russia, Iran and Cuba, as well as Brazil, Italy and Quebec due to "local regulations." For developers not in those areas, applications for the grant are open until December 18th, with the recipients to be notified by the end of February 2027. If you're a developer who's interested, you can apply here.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard.
  • Recent findings suggest that for those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the latest late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold.
  • According to recent reports, there was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard. Suspensions have been issued, trade locks have been put on accounts, and ill-gotten gold is being seized.

Recent findings suggest that for those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the latest late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold. By quickly clearing select mobs with area-of-effect damage, players would loot upwards of 100 raw gold an hour. This exploit, clearly not intentional, was nonetheless farmed until Blizzard hotfixed it earlier in the week.

According to recent reports, there was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit. That speculation would come to an end late last night with an official statement from the World of Warcraft: Forever development team.

Recent findings suggest that "As players continue their journey into WoW Forever’s higher-level content, we are closely monitoring the game economy to ensure that gold sources and costs are well balanced," the statement reads. "Finding efficient farming spots has always been part of the game, and is how most players have earned their epic mounts since 2004. When a single location proves so lucrative that it overshadows all other sources, we generally adjust it to bring it in line with the rest.".

In a recent development, it goes on to explain the nature of the bug that made this gold farm possible, before reassuring those who may have accidentally benefited from some extra cash from their regular runs of Blackmaw Hold they have nothing to worry about. The same cannot be said for those who took advantage of the situation.

"Players who simply ran Blackmaw Hold a few times and benefited organically from the extra loot did nothing wrong, and no one should worry that they’re putting their account at risk if they accidentally benefit from a bug," it continues. "But there were a couple hundred players worldwide who recognized that this was unintended and spent significant time exclusively farming that group of enemies.

"Yesterday, we put an economy lock on their accounts to prevent broader impact to the game economy while we investigated the extent of the exploitative gains, including gold earned by vendoring bugged drops. Today, we are in the process of removing all such gold earned, as well as applying account suspensions to significant abusers.".

It has been revealed that the post concludes by thanking players for their feedback on the matter, and a final warning: "As always, we advise all players to refrain from abusing game mechanics that are clearly unintended. We will continue to take action against intentional abuse.".

This decision certainly sets the precedent moving forward with World of Warcraft: Forever that such exploits won't be tolerated, and rolling back the wealth of those who made out of Blackmaw Hold like bandits is a good measure that should prevent continuous damage.

According to recent reports, inevitably the exploit would have had some impact, specifically in those days prior to trading blocks being put in place. While the gold on the exploiter's accounts may be removed, any purchases they made on the in-game auction house will have affected others through buying and selling goods with ample funds.

Those who were suspended temporarily will be able to regain access to the game by the time the first wave of raids come out in December, so it very much feels like a firm slap on the wrist in that regard. Even so, given the establishment of punishments for such behavior, one can only wonder if future events will come with harsher penalties.

According to recent reports, world of Warcraft: Forever, despite this small economic roadbump, is proving exceptionally popular for Blizzard. It's already broken records for the series, and has impressed players so far with its revamping of the classic MMO.

Konami has provided zero indication that it aims to bring any Silent Hill games to the Switch 2, so while we wallow in despair, we can at least take comfort in the knowledge that something remarkably similar is on the way.

Revealed at The Horror Game Awards 2026, Ugly Within is published by Serafini Productions and confirmed for Switch 2, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC. There's no release date as of yet, but judging from the quality of the trailer, it seems development is proceeding well.

Featuring a familiar over-the-shoulder viewpoint, Ugly Within sees you take on the roles of Shu Onodera and Reiko Miyama as they investigate the mysterious Kamata estate. The former utilises stealth abilities to slip by monsters unseen, while the latter confronts them head-on via exorcism.

The trailer is unsettling, to say the least, and the production value seems high. There's one sequence in which a woman's face just peels open to reveal a bulging eye surrounded by teeth, and it's proper gross.

Let's check out the key features:.

- See the Past: Use Shu's ability to read the echoes left in rooms and objects, uncovering clues from the past to solve present-day mysteries.

- Two Protagonists: Switch between stealth, quiet exploration and puzzle-solving as Shu and direct confrontation and exorcism as Reiko.

- Secluded Estate: Explore a traditional Japanese house filled with dim corridors, tatami rooms and hidden underground spaces, each holding a piece of the Kamata family's story.

- Survival Under Pressure: Follow the records and traces others left behind, manage limited resources and find a way to survive what the family has been hiding.

According to recent reports, so yes, while we continue to lament the lack of Silent Hill on Switch 2, we'll keep a close eye on Ugly Within in the coming weeks and months. It looks neat, and hopefully it'll prove a worthy alternative upon release.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the GTA 6 Kit Car locations are spread all over Leonida, making your search to repair Wyman's fourth car significantly more involved than the Transgressor, Riata, or even the Mamba GT. There are five whole cars to scan with the WAiNK It app, but it's well worth it, because the Kit Car is super fast and stylish.

It's worth noting that you'll need to complete the Chapter 3 mission, Meet the Heders, to acquire the cut-off tool (since one of the Kit Cars is in a locked shipping container). After the Kit Car, there's one additional vehicle in the Classic Car Collection, the Deviant, but it doesn't actually require a collectible hunt as Wyman will simply offer it to you, making this your last one.

In a recent development, the first Kit Car is inside the garage at Willie's Service Center in south Vice City, southeast of Salton, and northwest of Tequesta. Just north of the purchasable 7th Avenue Garage and west of Vice City Firearms,you'll spot a building on the left labelled as Willie's Service Center with a brown top half and blue lower half.

Enter the ground floor via the door around the left side by the stairs. You'll have to break in, which sounds an alarm, so be quick scanning the car inside.

The second one is on Casanova Island, the rightmost of the Rialto Islands that connect west Vice City with east Vice City. When you reach the island, driving west to east (coming from Vespucci) head along the northernmost road and look to your left about halfway across the island for a major white villa with a small gated garage next door—it's next to a big vacant lot. Push the gate open to find the kit car right in front of you.

It has been revealed that the third one is in a shipping container on Wild Hog Point, directly to the southwest of Port Gellhorn, on the big peninsula that sticks out where the airfield is located. For this one, you'll need to have completed the Meet the Heders mission in Chapter 3 to acquire the cut-off tool to open it.

Industry observers note that it's on the westernmost edge of the point, around the middle of the pools that look a bit like a seahorse on the map. Due to the end of Chapter 2, similar to Grassrivers, this area is also a hot spot for police, so be careful while driving around. Look for the yellow scoop container, crack it open, and scan the car inside.

Industry observers note that the fourth one is around the back of Donnie's Auto Repair Watson Bay in Watson Bay town, west of Hamlet, southwest of Port Gellhorn. This garage (which has Donnie's Auto Repair written on it) is next door to the Pay 'n' Spray - Watson Bay. Just head around the left side of the building and you'll find the Kit Car to scan immediately on your right.

The fifth Kit Car is in a fancy garage on the west side of Capri on the little curving northern peninsula of houses. Capri is south of Port Gellhorn on the coast. Drive along the road until you spot the building site on your right and the green villa on your left—just after it, you'll find the driveway of the house you want, also on the left. Follow the path and break into the garage on your right to find the car.

Same as always, wait for Wyman to finish the car and call, then click the payment request he sends in his following text to Buck him $1,500 before collecting the car from the nav point at his scrapyard.

It has been revealed that this is actually the final car hunt, as later Wyman will call you and straight-up ask if you want the final car, a Deviant. You then pay him $1,000 for labour, and it's immediately yours to collect, so with this, you've basically finished the Classic Car Collection.

Animal Crossing: Latest Horizons has received a surprise patch today to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the life sim series. The update, version 3.0.2, is available across the Switch and Switch 2 versions of the game.

According to recent reports, the patch brings a single fresh addition to New Horizons - a leaf item. Everyone gets it, too, so you don’t have to do anything special to acquire it.

After installing the patch, simply head to your in-house mailbox to claim it. The mail includes a hearty message to fans who supported the series for years, featuring an appropriate Nintendo N64 stamp.

April 14, 2011 marks the release of the original, lesser-known version of Animal Crossing in Japan. The game was initially released as Animal Forest (Dobutsu no Mori) on the Nintendo N64, before later making its way to the Nintendo GameCube in December of the same year as Dobutsu no Mori+ with some extra features.

That same, original design of the package is also available for display in your game. The rest of the patch notes are entirely about various bug fixes, so not much more there. You can see the full change log on Nintendo’s support website.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As part of a summit meeting in Manchester yesterday, the IWGB Game Workers union have joined up with other unions spanning the Republic of Ireland's GWUI, Germany's GDRT, Italy's FIOM-CGIL, France's STJV, and Spain's CSVI to publish a manifesto that aims to "bring to light the risks and dangers genAI poses to the workforce" for consumers, workers and publishers alike.

Sources indicate that the manifesto states that "GenAI is presently harming the games industry, its workers and the games they produce," and suggests actions that can be taken by all to reduce harm done to the industry. The manifesto specifies the "severe harm to the environment, the destruction of communities and the exploitation of the Global South" as wider harms of the technology, but maintains its focus on the industry itself.

The effects of the technology on gamemakers, such as "directly and indirectly replacing workers", "worker fatigue, cognitive decline and burnout", and "a marked decline in junior positions in the industry" are listed as core harms to be avoided and fought against, with the manifesto also noting that it also "removes a sense of ownership from workers [...] the things they produce no longer feel like they have the workers' stamp on them, and therefore they can no longer take pride in them." As it states, "games are best made by people.".

The manifesto goes on to explains the unions' stance that genAI is "sold to employers as an alternative to workers", and its "predisposition towards sycophancy and lack of real world context can lead to an increase in unreasonable, damaging requests when used by employers to set policy, timescales, workloads, etc., as well as to task expansion and a general degradation of conditions." In addition, its nature as a tool built on the theft of stolen third-party data is highlighted as an inherent danger, and the so-called loophole in only training models on internal data is equally highlighted as resulting in employees and creators rarely being credited or compensated for their work that is fed into the machine. This issue also ties into the inherent implicit and explicit discrimination that exists in genAI content due to datasets' "intrinsic and exclusionary Western bias that limits diversity and marginalises non-dominant languages, cultures, and ethnicities", which leads to "a homogenisation of culture.".

As for action, the manifest recommends that workers should "avoid usage of genAI services whenever possible", "distance yourself from genAI usage", and "make it clear to your employer why you do not want to use genAI", as well as, of course, to "organise. Unionise. Do it now, not when it is too late and you are already under threat." Similarly, employers are recommended to "ensure that no worker is required to use genAI", and to "disallow the use of genAI in the organization code of conduct, even for early stages of development." Finally, for consumers, it simply advises to "support games made without genAI", and to "be vocal about disliking genAI in games.".

It's an incredibly clear and concise statement that calls to mind the statement made by a selection of IGF jurors on the state of genAI in the industry and their decision not to vote for any game that uses genAI in any capacity. As both of these statements are joined in saying, "we do not have to accept the use of genAI to make video games; it is not inevitable.".

When games have, let's say, a worldwide release time of midnight across all nations, those living in New Zealand are able to jump in first as a result.

It has been revealed that microsoft has for years been happy to let this practice continue on its platform, and as such a sort of cultural norm about hopping on a digital plane for a game's release has been established. #97751. Breaking: I'm not saying Sleeping Dogs is the world's best life of crime sim, but no other game has replicated the importance of pork buns to whole manhood as deftly

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1289 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: I'm not saying Sleeping Dogs is the world's best life of crime sim, but no other game has replicated the importance of pork buns to whole manhood as deftly

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1289 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, for absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again.
  • Tonally and in terms of setting, Sleeping Dogs feels a lot closer to GTA 4’s gritty urban gangland drama than Rockstar’s follow-up did.
  • According to recent reports, for Wei, it’s a balancing act between his day-to-day life surviving among the triads, and keeping his hands clean while securing evidence against them as an undercover cop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, for absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again. The United Front Games-developed, Square Enix-published open-world crime romp is still as good as it’s always been, and still occupies its own corner in the dingy bar where the GTAs and GTA-likes hang out. Back in 2015, RPS co-founderman Alec Meer (RPS in peace) referred to it as “the halfway house between GTA's sneering arrogance and Saints Row's chaotic nonchalance”. Fair enough, I’ve never been that massive a Saints Row guy, but I see slumbering canines a bit differently.

Tonally and in terms of setting, Sleeping Dogs feels a lot closer to GTA 4’s gritty urban gangland drama than Rockstar’s follow-up did. GTA 5 is an exotic and sun-kissed heist movie, a mould that GTA 6’s tale of gun-toting love in Vice City very much looks to follow. That leaves Sleeping Dogs protagonist Wei Shen standing next to Niko Bellic. One might be kicking faces in Hong Kong and the other might be getting into shootouts in New York, but both are fresh off the boat in places both familiar and alien. They find themselves caught between two lives.

According to recent reports, for Wei, it’s a balancing act between his day-to-day life surviving among the triads, and keeping his hands clean while securing evidence against them as an undercover cop. For Niko, it’s a balancing act between trying to settle old scores and start a fresh life in post 9/11 America. One can stop at a street vendor to buy a pork bun to chow down on. One can stop at a street vendor to buy a hotdog to chow down on. Both of their games are beloved for delivering tales which get the player invested in Wei and Niko specifically, that excel in putting you into the emotional shoes of these two underworld operators whose worlds are tearing at them from multiple angles as they claw their way to the top of the food chain.

Despite my headline gag, they do this with a comparably minimal amount of in-depth life-simmy details, like those that’re baked into Red Dead Redemption 2 (and GTA 6, to a degree) as some of the main selling points. Wei can buy a pork bun, the vendor loudly informs him that by doing so he’s avoiding the possibility of never becoming a whole man, but there’s no ‘whole manliness’ meter which demands to be satiated with regular pork bun munching, lest Wei become a less than whole man. All it does is give him a temporary health regeneration boost, because as we all know, the first thing the doctors do if you’re admitted to hospital with grievous wounds after a fight is serve you a scrumptious meal that miraculously closes up your cuts in minutes.

Sleeping Dogs dedicates all of its life simming effort to making you feel the weight of Wei’s torment as he grapples with an unsustainable double life of sinning and saintly acts. Like GTA 4, it’s not got the time, tech, or budget to adorn itself with animations or systems that replicate every aspect of Wei’s day-to-day existence in excruciating detail. It’s simply assumed, rather than demonstrated, that some of the back alleys he wanders down to bust drug dealers probably smell a bit unpleasant. He doesn’t have over 60 species of bird to catalogue as he commutes from North Point to the businessman-infested Central district, then on to the houseboat-heavy Aberdeen and gated communities of Kennedy Town. Though, he does keep nicking jade statues, in order to persuade his kung fu instructor to teach him some fun fresh ways to knee baddies into submission.

He can sing his lungs out to nail I Fought the Law at one of Hong Kong’s few karaoke booths or lose all of his cash playing mahjong, but he doesn’t have an endless laundry list of optional hobbies long enough to suck players who aren’t even particularly trying to get distracted in for hundreds of hours.

According to recent reports, then again, if he wanders into his Central apartment, Wei can take a piss. In truth, I’d forgotten about this prior to my recent revisit, but it is a wonderfully simple feature that really emphasises how things’ve changed for games like these in the years since 2012. I press one button when the prompt pops up near the loo, and Wei unzips before dribbling a rather loud trickle into the bowl. Then, he’s done. I can get him to wash his hands if I wish, but no bladder meter has gone down and no dirtiness meter is being satiated by my scrubbing. If Wei doesn’t take regular whizzes, no NPCs comment that he’s looking a bit pained, and his walking animation doesn’t dynamically adjust to huddle his legs closer together.

It has been revealed that you could ask what was even the point of animating Wei’s pissing if it’s a pointless and totally optional activity, outside of arguably doing a tiny bit of work in helping Shen be convincingly human (and it unquestionably being quite funny the first time you stumble across it). By looping what would once have been one-note button presses into systems that help them play a more active role in fleshing out the world and the routines of its inhabitants, uber-detailed games like GTA 6 - at their best - add an extra layer of definition to the tales and adventures they depict.

It has been revealed that they often feel like the sort of game Sleeping Dogs might’ve been if it’d had their tech and its budget was the GDP of real world Hong Kong. The question is, when limitations like that don’t apply to the degree they once did, where the line lies between extra layers which tangibly deepen the player’s experience and overindulgent bloat?

Recent findings suggest that sleeping Dogs, despite working in its own takes on elements of GTA, Saints Row, and I’d argue RGG Studio’s earlier Like A Dragon/Yakuza entries, is an unquestionably lean and focused game. Less isn’t necessarily more, especially if you were to ask slumbering canines-loving teenage me, who would’ve bitten your hand off for Hong Kong to boast even a third of the extra features and activities GTA 6 and Red Dead 2 pack into their life of crime sims.

The latter two are games that wouldn’t have been possible to make, at least in a format the masses would be able to play, back in the era when Sleeping Dogs and GTA 4 represented what an open-world crime game typically looked like. They’ve eaten up what used to be the domain of arcade racers like Midnight Club and hunting sims to step closer to being something reminiscent of Better Than Life, the addictive VR everything game from the Red Dwarfverse, which takes over players’ lives by simulating a world where everything they want can play out in reality-mimicking detail.

In a recent development, they aim to be far, far more than what defined their predecessors, and to use that to appeal to an ever-expanding audience. What I’m intrigued to see, whenever I get my hands on Rockstar’s latest work, is whether those like me who come to it having recently played a game like Sleeping Dogs will find a game that feels like it’s being pulled in a million different directions, to the point that it loses something of what historically has been at the centre of its fundamental appeal.

Or, to put it another way: is there a point at which you’ve eaten so many pork buns in one sitting that you begin to stray away from the self-actualisation which steady consumption of them is known to facilitate?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Metro series is finally, officially back with a new installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

Sources indicate that what won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The new protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

Today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that there are a lot of secrets and collectibles hidden throughout Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • Two of these are the Guardia Brothers FRA legendary assault rifle and Benefactor sports car, both of which are obtainable at the same location!
  • If you want to get this legendary assault rifle and sports car, you will need to first head to Vice City and then go to the Little Cuba district.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there are a lot of secrets and collectibles hidden throughout Grand Theft Auto 6. These can range from simple easter eggs to comically elaborate puzzles you'll need to solve. However, some just require a bit of criminal activity to earn some great rewards.

Two of these are the Guardia Brothers FRA legendary assault rifle and Benefactor sports car, both of which are obtainable at the same location! If you're looking to snag a few grand, a newly introduced car, and a weapon, here is where to find them and how to get these legendary items.

If you want to get this legendary assault rifle and sports car, you will need to first head to Vice City and then go to the Little Cuba district. In the northeast corner of Little Cuba there will be a gated house that a black van will pull into if you get close. This doesn't always happen, and your ability to rob this area isn't determined by the van showing up, so don't fret.

It has been revealed that while you can try to just bust through the front gate, you can actually sneak in over the wall. Head to the right of the gate along the spiked wall (shown above) until you reach a section near the back that can be climbed over. I strongly recommend doing this, as you can basically eliminate every gang member without raising an alarm so long as you have a silenced weapon.

Once you reach the backyard, ignore the legendary Benefactor car for now and head up the scaffolding along the side of the building to the roof. Climb through the open hatch and equip your silenced weapon. Below you will be four gang members sitting around a table on the ground floor. Additionally, there is one other criminal rummaging through a safe on the second floor.

It has been revealed that take out your silenced weapon, activate Focus mode, and eliminate all four criminals on the first floor before they can react. If you're fast enough, all of them can be killed without alerting anyone outside or even the guy looking in the safe! With the four gang members dead, use your Focus and look at the floor by the ladder.

Industry observers note that this will reveal a secret stash area that has some cash you can loot. There is also a high-end watch on the table to your left along with some Sticky Bombs, which you will need to escape. When you're ready, head down to the second floor and knock out the guy putting money into the safe. Take all the cash and go to the bottom floor.

Industry observers note that there you will find a mix of money, marked bills, and jewelry. Stuff your bag full of valuables, loot the bodies, and look for a small armory to the right of the front entrance. In a weapon case, you will find the Guardian Brothers FMA assault rifle. Once you've thoroughly ransacked the place, take everything out the back door to where the Benefactor is.

In a recent development, store your items in the truck of the car, take out your silenced weapon, and kill the guard who is standing along the driveway near the gate. With him dead, approach the gate at the end of the driveway, attach a sticky bomb to the side when prompted, and shoot the two guards on the other side of the gate. Blow open the gate, then run up to the switch to open the main gate so you can drive out (circled above).

This should allow you to escape without triggering a single gunfight or having the police called on you. Now you can take the Benefactor and get it registered at someone like Moses for a little over $3,800. This ensures you can call the car anytime you need it, making it yours for the rest of the game.

It has been revealed that diablo 4 is mere days away from the launch of its biggest expansion yet, and Blizzard wants to make sure it got one last chance to tell you about it. Lord of Hatred is the follow-up to 2024’s Vessel of Hatred, and it’s set to arrive on April 28.

Next week, however, we’re getting an updated look at the new content as part of a livestream. This is the Developer Patch kind; the meaty, information-dense show anyone who follows Diablo’s livestreams should be familiar with.

According to recent reports, the next Developer Patch is set for Thursday, April 23. It’ll kick off at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 6pm GMT. The show will, naturally, focus on Lord of Hatred. In particular, we’re getting another look at the expansion content that hasn’t been given the same level of coverage as the bigger features.

Everyone knows about the new Skovos region, the Warlock class (and the Paladin before that), but we haven’t seen much from the other gameplay-altering features that affect a lot of the core flow.

In next week’s showcase, Blizzard will show off the updated and expanded skill trees - which come to all classes, the Talisman system, and the gear-altering Horadric Cube. War Prepares, the newly introduced make-your-own-endgame feature will be discussed, too.

In a recent development, more interestingly, we’re also going to hear about the upcoming season kicking off right alongside the launch of Lord of Hatred. A short, in-betweener season is currently live in Diablo 4, and it’s going to end right as the next one/the expansion launch.

And, of course, the show won’t end before the team takes a few questions from chat, as is tradition. If you want to catch it live, you’ll be able to do so on Diablo’s official YouTube, Twitch, Twitter, and TikTok channels.

Gloomwood, the Victorian survival horror immersive sim (or, wait, I'm getting reports that we shouldn't call it an immersive sim, apparently) by Dillon Rogers is a game that is quite happily inspired by its predecessors such as Thief, Resident Evil and Dishonored; you could call it 'Thief with guns', if you really wanted to. (Sorry, I've just seen that the domain for Gloomwood's site used to be 'residenthievil.com'. Wonderful). Now, that last inspiration has come full circle, as publisher New Blood Interactive's latest revision post confirms that the newest member of the team is none other than former Dishonored designer Julien Eveillé.

In addition to his work at Arkane on Dishonored and its sequel, Deathloop, and even Marvel's Blade, Eveillé also developed his own indie horror, 2024's short and sweet Threshold. It's quite a legacy to add to this team, and his hiring is described by New Blood as an example of how "finding level designers who are up to the task of working on Gloomwood is not easy". The post also mentions that Eveillé will be added alongside "our new devs", implying that he's not the only new addition to the team.

It has been revealed that other than these new hires, the patch is set to include quite a bit to change up Gloomwood and make it bigger. The highlight is the First National Bank level, which is described as "our largest and most intricately designed level yet", with the screenshots showing off a grand and imposing, yet claustrophobic in places, that makes the act of going to the bank even more intimidating than usual. The Bank is joined by the new stun prod weapon, which is self-explanatory, and the new Rat and Fishdog transformations, which let you sneak through crawlspaces and swim through dirtied waters respectively. That sneaking will be made more difficult by the addition of alarms and blood pools that both alert surrounding guards to your presence, though the new Crow King transformation offers a new, acid-belching way to take down any guards that come running.

It has been revealed that the enhancement is tentatively scheduled for "before the end of the year", but New Blood aren't setting down a specific release date. Rogers himself will also be going through back surgery very soon, for which I wish him a gentle recovery and, hopefully, as easy a return to work as possible.

Slay the Spire 2 is one of this year's best selling games despite only being available on PC, and its players are "obsessed"

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (466 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One million copies for each month on sale, it seems.
  • That's according to estimates by Alinea Analytics industry analyst Rhys Elliott, who revealed in a LinkedIn post that those sales translate to $157.6m (~£119.6m) in revenue for the small studio.
  • Slay the Spire 2 is now the sixth best-selling 2026 release across Steam, PlayStation and Xbox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One million copies for each month on sale, it seems. Slay the Spire 2, Mega Crit's roguelike deckbuilder, is estimated to have sold 7.9m copies since its release in Steam Early Access in March.

That's according to estimates by Alinea Analytics industry analyst Rhys Elliott, who revealed in a LinkedIn post that those sales translate to $157.6m (~£119.6m) in revenue for the small studio.

Slay the Spire 2 is now the sixth best-selling 2026 release across Steam, PlayStation and Xbox. That is notable, as the game is only out on Steam, meaning it has sold enough copies to outpace games on platforms it's not even available on.

We already knew Slay the Spire 2 was one of the year's biggest releases. In its first week on sale, the game sold over 3m copies. It quickly became March's top-selling game on Steam, beating blockbuster competition in Crimson Desert and Resident Evil Requiem. Slay the Spire 2, alongside other indie titles such as Meccha Chameleon, have helped Steam deliver another record year of revenue.

It was such a hit, even, that other indie developers felt it negatively impacted sales of their own games. Mewgenics maker Edmund McMillen recently told Eurogamer "it sucked everybody out". "The same players who liked Mewgenics, they were Slay The Spire players. So they all went woosh and right over," McMillen remarked.

Slay the Spire 2 has been consistently popular with players, too, and that popularity has seemingly continued. Elliott noted the game never fell below 2.5 million active players each month since March.

Slay the Spire 2's loyal following also meant that the recently released beta patch, which added a newly introduced character, was enough to bring back millions of players. Despite only being available for players who opt into the beta branch of the game, Slay the Spire 2 more than doubled its daily active users to reach its highest daily player count in six months.

"Simply put: Slay the Spire 2 players are obsessed," wrote Elliott. "And it's not just a niche group of dedicated players, either. The average play time is nearly 84 hours, sure. But zooming out, 1.9 million folks have played for over 100 hours.".

Incidentally, nearly 100,000 players bought the game but never played it, which Elliott added could explain the discrepancy between player numbers and copies sold.

Looking ahead, Slay the Spire 2's road to version 1.0 is expected to be long, with several features and gameplay additions still in the works. Then there are the console ports, which have yet to be unveiled, but are very much expected.

In Eurogamer's Slay the Spire 2 early access review, Bertie Purchese called it "a deceptively familiar sequel" whose confident design and smart fresh additions build on what made the original work so well.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This latest feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a new premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

For most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis noted that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

It has been revealed that interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

Unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

Considering the Marketplace only just launched on consoles, the company may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the new paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that there are more secrets, references, and easter eggs in GTA 6 than we can possibly know.
  • There are electronics stores dotted all over Leonida, but on the shelves of one called Game Horde that can be found in the Port Gellhorn region of the map, there are video games.
  • There are a few games on the shelf, most of which appear to be GTA 6 versions of real-life titles, although the most obvious is the We Came Together collection.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there are more secrets, references, and easter eggs in GTA 6 than we can possibly know. We will almost certainly be stumbling on them for years to come. A lot have been discovered during these first few days, though, including what is almost certainly a friendly jab at Naughty Dog for its many remasters and remakes of The Last of Us games.

There are electronics stores dotted all over Leonida, but on the shelves of one called Game Horde that can be found in the Port Gellhorn region of the map, there are video games. Not video games that exist in our world, or would even be compatible with our consoles, but all are references to real games and compatible with the JoySystem, the in-universe console you can play back at your house after Cal sets it up in the early stages of the game.

There are a few games on the shelf, most of which appear to be GTA 6 versions of real-life titles, although the most obvious is the We Came Together collection. Not only do the name and the font confirm that it's the Vice City version of The Last of Us, but Rockstar has had a little fun at Naughty Dog’s expense with the easter egg.

Under the game name along the case’s spine, it reads “I, II, & III Remasters of the Remakes”. Clearly a little dig at Naughty Dog for repeatedly re-releasing the first two Last of Us games rather than making a new one. The Last of Us has a rematser and a remake, The Last of Us Part 2 has already been remastered, and both Part 1’s remake and Part 2’s remaster were re-released as a double-pack.

Recent findings suggest that you might argue that it’s pretty rich of Rockstar to make that joke when it released GTA 5 across three different consoles, it just never gave its GTA 6 predecessor the remaster label. Even when taking that into account, though, Naughty Dog has given its games more remasters and remakes, even though the original The Last of Us was released only three months before GTA 5.

The GTA 6 equivalent of The Last of Us Part 3 is also already available in Leonida. We’ll be waiting another decade for the real thing, at least.

In a recent development, the other JoySystem games on the shelf are Desolate Rim, which is Death Stranding based on the font, Righteous Slaughter is GTA’s Call of Duty, and Glory Souls 2. Clearly a FromSoftware game, but it’s unclear which one. The name suggests Demon’s Souls, but the font screams Elden Ring.

GTA 6 players have spent almost 80,000 years collectively in-game already, so it’s no wonder these tiny details are already being discovered. What’s even more remarkable, considering that timeframe, is how much more we still haven’t seen.

Update [Mon 23rd Nov 2026, 2:20pm]: Nvidia has posted an update confirming that Jensen Huang has now been reinstated as president, CEO, and board member following his earlier resignation.

Sources indicate that the post confirms that Nvidia's board "received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk".

Huang resigned following multiple instances of alleged infidelity, most notably with an alleged Chinese spy, leading to concerns over national security as the US and China butt heads in the race to become the dominant force in the world of AI.

Huang also contributed the following message.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution. I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period.

"I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”.

We can only assume that the investigation into Huang's relationships turned up nothing unusual – surely they wouldn't just sweep it under the rug, right?

Meanwhile, US president Donald Trump celebrated Huang's reinstatement, calling him a "Great Patriot and National Treasure" while stating that the decision is vital to "ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Firm, but the American Economy".

Original Story: Nvidia, one of the largest tech firms in the world and the tech giant responsible for the Switch 2's custom processor, has found itself embroiled in scandal over recent days.

As reported by The Guardian, Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang, who you might recognise from the 'Creator's Voice Special Edition' video for Switch 2, has now resigned after reported affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and a company employee.

He will be replaced on an interim basis by Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, until a full-time successor is named. Nvidia's share price began to sharply decline following reports of the scandal, to the point where it is now no longer the most valuable manufacturer in the world.

The BBC speculates that Huang's departure could set him up to be a "formidable opponent" to the very organization he co-founded, with Elon Musk stating that it would be "an honour" to work with him at SpaceX.

With regards to Nintendo, it's likely that none of this will have any immediate impact on Nvidia's relationship with the Japanese firm. Nvidia will no doubt be under contract to supply custom chips for the Switch 2, but what happens with the inevitable Switch 2 successor is under question.

Hopefully everything will go smoothly for Nintendo, but if it wants to utilise Nvidia's architecture for its next console – particularly for backwards compatibility – then its efforts may be impacted by Huang's departure along with Nvidia's sharp pivot towards AI.

Of course, it's really early to be speculating about the 'Switch 3', but you can bet that Nintendo's R&D department will be looking at all of this very closely and considering its potential impact.

Recent findings suggest that what are your thoughts on all of this? Could Huang's departure have any effect on Nvidia's business with Nintendo? Let us know with a comment.

I would hope that this isn't a case of Embracer cutting staff in the misguided hope that they can just be replaced with the use of genAI, but who can say. Solidarity to those affected, who I hope can find new work soon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last night, it was revealed that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's lead narrative designer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, won a BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her contribution to the hit 2025 game, which made history after winning 12 Game Award nominations last year. In the aftermath of her win, Svedberg-Yen dropped a pretty big bombshell: she's no longer with the game's developer, Sandfall Interactive.

"No, I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition," she told Gamesbeat when asked if she's still with the firm. "We've parted ways." As to what Svedberg-Yen is doing next, she offered a cryptic answer, including talk of writing "my own projects, my own stories". She also discussed another project she's set her sights on: establishing a fund to help mentor and grow a new generation of video game narrative designers.

"One of the initiatives I want to build is a narrative investment fund to focus on narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers," she explained, noting her background working in finance and how that dovetails nicely with her more recent experience as a narrative lead. "This is the chicken and egg question a lot of people face. To get money from publishers you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors.".

In a recent development, her motivation for this initiative? Simply, she wants to change how the industry works. "I've discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it's a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations.".

Recent findings suggest that "The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help," she added later. "That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don't know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry.".

Recent findings suggest that sandfall Interactive previously said its guiding "North Star" will always be its "own personal taste", and what the team enjoys.She noted that she didn't think the studio would bow to pressure from fans to do more of the same, but instead be guided by what it thinks is best for itself, and for the series. "I've seen too many TV shows and books be swayed trying to please a lot of people, and in the process you end up losing the heart of what's there," she noted.

We know that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is "not the end" of the franchise, and it seems that whatever happens next, it'll have at least a little bit of Svedberg-Yen's creativity instilled in it. I wish her the best for whatever her next step is.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a initiative laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons currently in the works, and a wealth of new additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging newly introduced video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

In a recent development, the video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

Recent findings suggest that we’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is stated to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

Industry observers note that the introduction of naval combat will bring with it a new dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

In a recent development, perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lots of people will tell you that Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos marks the series' first female protagonist. Lots of people are, of course, wrong. GTA 1 had eight selectable protagonists, four of whom were women, while GTA 2 for the Game Boy Color let you play protags Candy or Gretchen (along with a bunch of other men) in addition to the PlayStation game's default Claude Speed.

Industry observers note that that vital pedantry out of the way, it's undeniable that Lucia is GTA's first female protagonist since the series became the culture-swallowing goliath it is today. In a chat with CBC's As It Happens, GTA OG Brian Baglow said he reckons it's "long, long overdue".

Recent findings suggest that baglow, credited as a writer on the original GTA and who served as "head of propaganda and indoctrination" at DMA Design (the studio that would become Rockstar North) in the '90s, said that back in the day of GTA 1, the devs didn't even have a script. "We started with a tech demo, a way of moving around a city… I came in to actually add the story, add the script, after the levels had been built".

That was mostly a process of, shall we say, finding inspiration: "we were making it up as we went along… it was a case of going into every crime movie, every heist, every caper, every TV show, cop show, crime drama, and lifting elements that I hoped would resonate with people".

It has been revealed that baglow sounds, rightfully, rather proud of his time spent working on such an crucial series, but he has his qualms as he casts his eye back over it. "The representation of women, it has not been good, and that's putting it very mildly", he claims, "so I'm delighted that we now have not only a female protagonist, but a Hispanic female protagonist. I think it's been long, long overdue, and I can't wait to get to grips with the game and see how in-depth it goes.

"I think it's showing a level of maturation because from the very earliest days it was a very young group of almost entirely male developers in Scotland".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that it's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony.
  • As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.
  • The lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the tech giant of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.

As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.

The lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers. Neill and co argued owning a PlayStation traps game buyers within a competitionless ecosystem, thereby impacting their ability to seek out a better deal.

It's quite similar to the arguments which have been made against Valve in similar lawsuits concerning the Steam overlords' dominance over the PC game buying space, though a key distinction is that there is some competition on PC via the likes of the Epic store and GOG. How effective some of that competition can be in practice is a different kettle of fish, but the options are there.

In a judgement that could potentially factor into the responses to any similar lawsuits against Valve or other PC storefronts going forwards, the tribunal ruled that Sony compete in a wider ‘systems market’ against Xbox, Nintendo and PC, with PlayStation having no legal duty under competition law to allow third-party stores onto their platform as competition closer to home. The latter the tribunal noted would be expensive, complex and come with potential security ramifications.

As if that wasn't enough, the body ruled that as far as the pricing being unfair went, Neill hadn't proven that Sony’s profit margins were excessive and declared there was no evidence the presence of rival storefronts on PlayStation would've seen prices come down. That's essentially the word NO written in the largest font possible on a sheet of paper the size of a table, then.

In a recent development, every lawsuit's different, especially when filed in different countries, but if I was one of the other class action suits against Sony or another massive game seller on the go at the moment, I'd maybe not be feeling so hot right now. On the other hand, perhaps seeing what the tribunal judged Neill not to have provided suffiencient evidence for might aid those other efforts in formulating their arguments ready to face the scrutiny of government bodies and corporate law-talkers.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Beleaguered Mindseye developer Build a Rocket Boy - the firm created by former Rockstar and Grand Theft Auto producer Leslie Benzies - apparently owes approximately £62 million in debt.
  • This came to light in a proposal issued by Build a Rocket Boy's administrators this week (spotted by Resetera), which lists both the moneys owed (right down to a £20 charge to OpenAI) and details what went wrong, as well as what Build a Rocket Boy intends to do to recoup money to pay the debts back.
  • "Prior to the Company's entry into Administration, the directors had been investigating circumstances surrounding the commercial performance of the video game, MindsEye, which was released in 2025 following significant development investment," the administration proposal read.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Beleaguered Mindseye developer Build a Rocket Boy - the firm created by former Rockstar and Grand Theft Auto producer Leslie Benzies - apparently owes approximately £62 million in debt. And a huge chunk of that appears to be owed to Chinese gaming company NetEase (£36.5m), though more than £1m appears to be owed to Benzies himself.

This came to light in a proposal issued by Build a Rocket Boy's administrators this week (spotted by Resetera), which lists both the moneys owed (right down to a £20 charge to OpenAI) and details what went wrong, as well as what Build a Rocket Boy intends to do to recoup money to pay the debts back. And the organization's "largest" potential asset, according to the administrators, is litigation.

"Prior to the Company's entry into Administration, the directors had been investigating circumstances surrounding the commercial performance of the video game, MindsEye, which was released in 2025 following significant development investment," the administration proposal read. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary.

Industry observers note that "The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that any such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions.".

Recent findings suggest that this tallies with the narrative spun by co-firm leader Mark Gerhard as the company waded into deep water. Gerhard blamed "organised espionage and corporate sabotage" for the studio's difficulties as multiple rounds of layoffs shredded Build a Rocket Boy. "People had their hands on the scale and deliberately tried to shape a negative narrative around the product," Gerhard said.

The situation he's referring to is likely the alleged smear campaign made against the game, which Gerhand reportedly claimed in an internal meeting this year was paid for by a "significant American organization" and then run by a UK company called Ritual Network, which apparently had influencers, journalists and staff at Build a Rocket Boy deliberately sabotage the game's release. That's according to an account of a videoed internal meeting reportedly seen by Insider Gaming earlier this year.

Industry observers note that it had nothing to do with the dire state of Mindseye when it rolled out, then. Eurogamer awarded it one out of five stars, chastising its "ridiculous story, inconsistent writing, poorly designed mission scenarios, and utterly atrocious combat" in our Mindseye review.

Recent findings suggest that build a Rocket Boy was founded in 2016, and its first game, Everywhere - a sort of online gaming platform - was revealed in 2022. It never materialised, but a part of that vision was carved out to become a standalone game experience of its own along the way, and that's how we got Mindseye - a take on a Grand Theft Auto formula. Whether or not the litigation is successful and can recoup any of Build a Rocket Boy's debts remains to be seen, but there's a financial mountain for the studio to climb if it hopes to operate again.

Recent findings suggest that the game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The fresh season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each new season.

Recent findings suggest that you’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Industry observers note that the even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The newly introduced season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

Industry observers note that blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

It has been revealed that in case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.
