Hours before it's even playable in most of the world, Grand Theft Auto 6 has already broken the record for the most viewers across livestreaming platforms like Twitch.

Sources indicate that according to streaming data and analytics website Streams Charts, GTA 6 had amassed 6.38m live viewers across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick at 12:30 UTC today. At that time, the game had been officially available for a few hours in Fresh Zealand, and elsewhere by using a region-switch trick.

The previous record for most live viewers was set by Valorant, Riot Game's popular tactical shooter, during its closed beta in xx. That game brought in 1.74m live viewers, but it's worth noting there was a promotion offering players a chance to access the beta if they watched a stream. Despite having no such incentive, GTA 6 has more than tripled Valorant's record.

Twitch is the largest platform for GTA 6 streams according to Streams Charts, and already the game is the 6th biggest category in Twitch history. It's also expected the figure will increase as GTA 6 rolls out officially in more regions of the world.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While GTA 6 has been receiving unbelievable praise and is technically considered one of the best video games of all time according to Metacritic, that certainly doesn't mean it's immune to criticism.

In a recent development, one of the substantial talking points both before and after launch has been that it's a 30FPS experience across all Xbox and PlayStation consoles, and if you're going from 60FPS back to 30FPS, there's definitely an adjustment period. Some people are absolutely fine with that, while others are finding it extremely difficult to go back.

For what it's worth, our friends at Digital Foundry have been analysing this in depth today:.

Rockstar Games has already confirmed recently that even the PS5 Pro doesn't come close to running GTA 6 at 60FPS due to the system's processor not being powerful enough, so we might be forced to wait until the next generation of consoles (and PC) before the game will become playable at 60 frames per-second.

Sources indicate that "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.”.

Sources indicate that with all of this in mind, we're interested to hear what you think about playing games at 30FPS on Xbox, PlayStation or anywhere else. It's becoming much more common that 60FPS is the default these days, but there are still some phenomenal 30FPS-only experiences out there, and it's a shame to think people are missing out on them.

I personally much prefer playing at 60FPS if I can, and there are certain games I will avoid at 30FPS until they get a patch down the line (like Mafia: Definitive Edition), but when it comes to industry-defining masterpieces like Red Dead Redemption 2 and Grand Theft Auto VI, the last thing I'd want is for them to scale back the detail in order to squeeze in a 60FPS mode.

So, what do you think? Tell us in the poll above and in the comments section below.

In a recent development, I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

Industry observers note that the stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

It's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

Getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that sharna Burgess isn't holding back on how she feels about Harry Shum Jr.'s shock elimination and the discourse around this season of Dancing With The Stars. As conversations continue about whether the show should allow contestants with professional dancing experience, she wants changes to the voting.

In a recent development, ahead of the finale on the 2026 TV schedule, Burgess was responding to questions from fans on her Instagram Stories. When asked if she was surprised by Shum Jr. being sent packing, this is what she had to say (via Us Magazine):.

Sadly no, I felt it was going to be another shock elimination. Not because they deserved it but simply because the online discourse is so wild that [it] was pretty clear who fans were ‘voting off’ and how they have felt about dance experience contestants.

In a recent development, the online fandom was going on in recent weeks about how unfair it was for Dancing With The Stars to have both Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Dewan in this season. That, paired with Tatyana Ali's continued improvement over the episodes, created a big discussion over whether it was better to watch dancers develop or ones who were already great.

The only way Ali was going to make the finals was for one fan-favorite to be sent home, and as improbable as it was, Harry Shum Jr. left over the remaining competitors. Sharna Burgess isn't the only DWTS cast member upset about the elimination, but she is one of the only ones calling for serious reform to the voting system:.

In a recent development, [It’s] so disappointing to see our voting system is now being used by viewers to vote people off instead of voting for your favorite. I say we got [sic] back to yall only have 10 votes total and you have to figure out how to dish them out. This voting ppl off thing is so insanely negative and not what we are built on and it’s seemingly given fans the chance to manipulate the show. JMO.

Recent findings suggest that sharna Burgess wants Dancing With The Stars to start limiting the voting and only giving fans ten votes, period, rather than ten per couple. Under this thinking, I'm assuming the idea is that viewers couldn't vote for everyone but the person they want eliminated. Would that be enough to turn things around?

Personally, I have doubts. To start, there's always the possibility that the voting can be tampered. For example, there was a massive rumor that Maura Higgins had to go to the hospital ahead of the semifinals, which might've impacted her votes from those who feared she'd be eliminated.

Sources indicate that plus, the obvious flaw in this strategy is that the viewers could still influence the vote and just encourage everyone else to vote for anyone but Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson. As I'd written previously, I think the solution is for DWTS to work toward equality between contestants as far as skill level.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

I'll be interested to see how the conversation continues after the finale, and how whoever is crowned the winner may shape it. There are already massive pushes online for Connor Wood to take home the big prize, and others hoping for Tatyana. All this before a single performance on the dance floor, which is another conversation entirely. Will there be changes to voting, or will this all blow over by the time next season rolls around?

Dancing With The Stars' Season 35 finale kicks off on ABC and Disney+ on Tuesday, November 24th at 8:00 p.m. ET. I'm ready to see who wins this Mirrorball Trophy by the end of Tuesday night.

Another moderator, TekS, also acknowledged that some user's posts may not be viewable as a result of ongoing strain on Reddit during GTA 6's release. They commented: "If you can't post/comment or see your user flair, well, know that it's perfectly normal.".

Recent findings suggest that ahead of the game's full launch across the world, the Grand Theft Auto 6 has already broken viewership records across streaming platforms like Twitch and YouTube. Interesting details about the game are also trickling out, including the fact that different refrigerators have their own unique sounds. Video games, ladies and gentlemen.

Sources indicate that with Grand Theft Auto 6 releasing today, our review has been released to the wild with it. It is overwhelmingly positive, with Chris Tapsell dubbing GTA 6 as "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made" and rated it a full five stars.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a substantial u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the company and AMERICA.

"On November 12th, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

Industry observers note that that last bit seems likely to have been remarked with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

Sources indicate that "Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.".

For now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board confirmed yesterday that they're establishing a "fresh standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the tech giant’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is presently serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the tech giant's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.

Where to find Auntie’s Place in GTA 6

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You'll need to find Auntie's Place in GTA 6 once you've get the laptop password to unlock Boogie’s laptop in the Chapter 3 safehouse.
  • To find Auntie’s Place in GTA 6, first head to Twa Ponya Tattoo parlour in the north of Vice City.
  • It has been revealed that the car isn’t at the restaurant itself.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You'll need to find Auntie's Place in GTA 6 once you've get the laptop password to unlock Boogie’s laptop in the Chapter 3 safehouse. The messages that gets you says there’s a surprise at Auntie’s Place, but there’s no hints as to where that is, and it’s not marked on the map as it’s not a place you can actually interact with.

To find Auntie’s Place in GTA 6, first head to Twa Ponya Tattoo parlour in the north of Vice City. Then, look across the street and you’ll see a small restaurant with a red sign. This is Auntie’s Place. It’s also around the back of Aline’s Thrift Store, if that helps.

It has been revealed that the car isn’t at the restaurant itself. Instead, behind and to the right of it there’s a locked garage. It may have a red car parked outside. You’ll automatically have the code you need to enter if you’ve unlocked Boogie’s laptop and read his messages. If not, you’ll need to head back to the apartment and take a look around for the clues hidden there. If you get stuck, we’ve also explained where you can find them and what words they hint towards.

Industry observers note that inside the garage you’ll find Vanessa's Growler, a pink Pfister (Porsche) sports car. The car will automatically be added to your owned vehicles. You’ll also unlock this garage as a place to store one vehicle. It’s called the Del Rio Boulevard Garage.

#97691. Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1296 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy 📈 Bullish 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1296 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the tech giant's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors.
  • BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals.
  • Industry observers note that build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the tech giant's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.

BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals. Asset manager Diameter Capital Partners are the second largest external creditor, having loaned BARB around £4.25 million. A further $19 million is owed to "group undertakings" – "group undertakings" meaning debts to parent companies, subsidiaries or fellow subsidiaries. Studio founder Benzies, meanwhile, is owed £1,158,167.05. Given that Benzies has been repeatedly accused of torpedoing MindsEye's fortunes by way of disruptive micro-management, I'm not sure many BARB staff would agree that he really deserves his million quid back at this stage, but that's what it says on paper. Smaller IOUs include £10,434.11 for Amazon Web Services, £634.36 for Unity, and a mighty £19.90 for OpenAI.

Industry observers note that build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say. Confirmed in 2023, their flagship project MindsEye is a filmic GTA-ish action shooter initially billed as a full-fat demo for Everywhere, a game creation platform comparable to Roblox. MindsEye struggled to compel us before launch and did not find its people on release, with poor sales leading to layoffs even as BARB leadership insisted they could revive the game's fortunes.

It has been revealed that the same leadership were subsequently accused by their own staff of "disastrously" mishandling the redundancies and enforcing "unbearable" crunch. Unionised BARB employees have now taken management to court for installing alleged surveillance software on their work PCs. The game's publishers Io Interactive noped out of the picture in March this year. Meanwhile, Benzies and Gerhard have thrown around accusations of a sinister espionage and sabotage campaign, carried out by unspecified perpetrators. They made a sort of revenge fantasy DLC pack about it, which our own Mark Warren characterised as we-already-have-Hitman-at-home. The bankruptcy documents shed more light on these twists and turns. According to the administrators, BARB were "funded mainly by equity investment from institutional, strategic and venture capital investors over several funding rounds, including a $110m Series D round in 2023." This followed a £32 million investment in 2020, as reported by GI. The firm grew significantly during MindsEye's creation to around 500 UK and overseas employees. According to a group income statement, the company posted sequential operating losses of £47.5 million for the period ending September 30th, 2025, and £63.1 million for the year ending December 2024. The administrator proposals document also devotes some time to the aforesaid allegations of sabotage. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary," it reads. "The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions." A later section vaguely alludes to the sum BARB leadership hope to recover. "Prior to the Joint Administrators' appointment, the Company had undertaken detailed investigations and had commenced litigation against several third parties, with the assistance of the Company's former legal advisers, Brandsmiths, in connection with matters described earlier in the Proposals," the doc reads. "The Joint Administrators consider the litigation potentially to be the largest asset of the Administration." The document goes on that BARB management have "sought financial support from third party investors to fund the anticipated legal costs and expenses associated with the litigation", with some of these funding agreements already executed. "Further executed agreements and associated funding contributions are expected to be received, shortly, and a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise," it continues. The Joint Administrators are "currently engaging in the on-going litigation, progressing the funding arrangements entered into by the Company, and have assessed the merits of pursuing the litigation". They will liaise with relevant parties to "determine the most appropriate strategy for preserving and, where appropriate, realising value from this potential asset for the benefit of creditors and other stakeholders." The doc doesn't name who, exactly, is being taken to court. As far as I'm aware, it isn't us. Anyway, it's good to know that the company who owe over £60 million are taking on more debt in order to pursue a histrionic grievance for which they have yet to supply any real evidence whatsoever.

Silent Hill, Fatal Frame Inspire This Promising Latest PS5 Horror Game

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (260 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Pushsquare

💡 Key Takeaways
  • You're probably describing at least half of the horror genre when you list Silent Hill and Fatal Frame as two of your main inspirations, but Ugly Within has cut through the crowded space with a reveal at The Horror Game Awards 2026.
  • In a recent development, it is in development for PS5, Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S, and PC, with no release window confirmed yet.
  • You play as two characters: Shu, a boy who can see into the past, and Reiko, an exorcist.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You're probably describing at least half of the horror genre when you list Silent Hill and Fatal Frame as two of your main inspirations, but Ugly Within has cut through the crowded space with a reveal at The Horror Game Awards 2026.

In a recent development, it is in development for PS5, Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S, and PC, with no release window confirmed yet. Catch it in action in the trailer above.

You play as two characters: Shu, a boy who can see into the past, and Reiko, an exorcist. It sounds like you'll be looking into a family history and confronting the ghost that has haunted it. Shu is a more stealthy character who avoids the supernatural and solves puzzles, while Reiko confronts the ghosts and exorcises them.

Shu and Reiko face the horrors of the Kamata estate in very different ways. Shu survives by staying unseen, moving through the house in silence and piecing together its secrets through visions of what once happened within its walls. Reiko meets the darkness head-on, confronting the entities that haunt the estate and driving them out through exorcism. But Shu's gift comes with a cruel limit: his visions reveal what happened to the people who came before, yet nothing he sees can be undone.

There is a touch of jank to the footage released so far, but the production quality overall appears to be really quite high. A lot like Perceptum, I think this one of the indie horror titles you need to keep an eye on.

Deciding whether to take the cut or pure drugs in GTA 6 is a decision you'll make during the Dealer's Choice mission in Chapter 3.

The proposal is that if you can pass off the drugs cut with baby powder, you can keep the profit, but the deal might go south if they realise, while bringing the pure stuff should make the dealers happy. Here's what happens if you choose either:.

According to recent reports, with that in mind, I'd say the cut drugs are the best to pick. You get maximum profit, a cool shootout that makes the mission less boring, and it doesn't have any significant consequences afterwards.

All 34 of the infamously fired Rockstar staff appear in GTA 6 game credits, though some aren't listed as "former employees", curiously

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • UPDATE 19TH NOVEMBER: All of the 34 fired Rockstar employees appear in the credits for GTA 6.
  • According to recent reports, also, we couldn't identify six names in the "former employees" section of the credits before because they don't appear there, we now know.
  • ORIGINAL STORY 18TH NOVEMBER: Eurogamer can confirm that at least 28 of the 34 employees fired by Rockstar roughly a year ago - in an action that directly led to the employment tribunal Rockstar is currently facing in Scotland - are named in the credits of Grand Theft Auto 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATE 19TH NOVEMBER: All of the 34 fired Rockstar employees appear in the credits for GTA 6. We were able to confirm the final few names' existence there after Rockstar posted the full credits online - in searchable form. Before this, the process of cross-checking was intensely laborious: it required watching a scrolling list of names for an hour-and-a-half to see if they appeared.

According to recent reports, also, we couldn't identify six names in the "former employees" section of the credits before because they don't appear there, we now know. These names appear listed under the departments the people worked for, as if they still worked at Rockstar. Why this is, we don't know - perhaps it's something to do with being involved in the employment tribunal or not. We're asking Rockstar for clarification.

ORIGINAL STORY 18TH NOVEMBER: Eurogamer can confirm that at least 28 of the 34 employees fired by Rockstar roughly a year ago - in an action that directly led to the employment tribunal Rockstar is currently facing in Scotland - are named in the credits of Grand Theft Auto 6.

Industry observers note that we cross-checked a list of 34 names supplied to us by the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain - the same organisation taking action against Rockstar on behalf of the fired employees. And of those names, we found 28 direct matches in the credits, along with a couple of discrepancies we've since verified, and some close-sounding names we're attempting to clarify. Some names may simply be missing. We won't publish the list for privacy reasons.

In a recent development, A number of those fired employees are seeking compensation for unfair dismissal amid allegations of "union busting", in an employment tribunal that comes to an end today. The delayed climax of the case couldn't be more fateful, aligned as it is with tomorrow's release of GTA 6, and the outcome will be historic either way.

Sources indicate that rockstar recently revealed that more than 4,711 people worked at the organization making GTA 6, employed across 12 offices around the world - a staff-count that has more than doubled since Red Dead Redemption 2. It's a game that's wowed critics - Eurogamer awarded GTA 6 five stars in our review this afternoon - and which observers expect to generate $2bn in revenue in its opening weekend alone.

But perhaps Christian Donlan put it best when digesting the opulence on display in the Netflix 'extended look' GTA 6 trailer. "To spend all this money making something so beautifully rich and detailed, to pay billions for this game and sweat every little animation, to float it out to us on Netflix, amongst genuine discussion around whether Netflix can handle it? That's commitment," he wrote. "And if you're willing to do that, and willing to do that to tell an underdog story, you should let your workers who made everything form a union.".
